name: Thomasina Bevan
languages: Spanish (learned from her pupils, and corrected by them daily)
equipment: A grey dust-coat over a black dress and a black bonnet, all of them practical and none of them new
Navy revolver (Colt, .36), her late husband's, 6 chambers loaded, which she has fired twice, both times at a mad dog
Pick handle, which she keeps by the schoolroom door for drunks and has used more often than the revolver
A Welsh Bible, an English hymnal and a Spanish primer she wrote herself for her pupils
A slate, chalk, and a register of forty-one pupils in four languages
A list in her own hand of every family at Plata Vieja and what the store owes them, or they owe the store
A Company handbill from Plata Vieja, yellow, folded small (from 5 July)
Mule: Jezebel, borrowed permanently from Con Hurley, who regrets it
features: Two Tongues (Immigrant origin: speaks, reads and writes Welsh and English, and Spanish well; advantage on Insight and Perception checks to follow a conversation in a language the speakers think she does not know; in any chapel or camp of people who share one of her languages she finds a meal, a bed and the news without a check)

Fire and Brimstone (Preacher, WIS: as an action, she preaches in a voice that carries over gunfire. Steady: each ally within 30 ft gains 1d6+4 temporary hit points and ends frightened and Shaken. Shake: each enemy within 30 ft who understands her makes a DC 14 WIS save or is frightened of her until the end of her next turn. 4 uses per short rest. No miracle in it: it works because people believe her)

Comfort the Afflicted (Preacher: stabilizes a dying creature as a bonus action with a DC 10 Medicine check, and it regains 1 hit point; once per short rest, ten minutes with someone grieving, frightened or ashamed ends Shaken and teaches her what truly troubles them)

The Flock (Preacher, 2nd level: wherever there is a chapel, a school or a gathering of decent people she finds shelter, a meal, news and someone to speak for her; once per town, an hour's preaching gives her +1 Reputation there until she leaves, or -1 to someone she preaches against by name, if the crowd believes her)

Calling: Shepherd (Preacher, 3rd level: Steady also gives each ally advantage on its next attack roll or saving throw before the end of its next turn, and Comfort the Afflicted can be used once per short rest)
Ability Score Improvement (Preacher, 4th level: +1 Constitution, +1 Wisdom)

The Schoolhouse (Schoolteacher background: the families of Plata Vieja trust her and tell her what they would not tell the sheriff, and their children, who see everything, tell her the rest; she reads and writes any document in English or Welsh, and most in Spanish)

personality.traits: I say exactly what I mean and expect other people to do the same, and I am disappointed daily. I sing when I am angry. I am kind to children and merciless to grown men who should know better.
personality.ideals: Every soul is worth the same to God and should be worth the same to the Company store. A man who is paid in scrip and voted like a sheep is being robbed twice.
personality.bonds: My forty-one pupils and their families. My husband Dafydd, buried at Plata Vieja in 1879 under a stone I paid for with a year's salary. The chapel at Merthyr where I was baptised, which I will never see again.
personality.flaws: I am certain I am right far more often than I am, and I do not forgive easily. I have been organising the miners into a union under Hamish Gow's nose, and I have not told them how dangerous that is.

appearance: A small, square, plain woman of forty-one with a weathered red face, sharp blue eyes behind steel spectacles, iron-grey hair under a black bonnet, and a voice much larger than she is. Grey dust-coat, black dress, sensible boots, and a pick handle she carries as some women carry a parasol.
backstory: Thomasina Bevan was born in 1840 in Merthyr Tydfil, in South Wales, the daughter of an ironworker and a chapel deacon, and she learned to read in the chapel's Sunday school and to preach, unofficially, in its prayer meetings, where women were allowed to speak if no man would. She married Dafydd Bevan, a coal miner, in 1862, and they came to America in 1869, to the coal fields of Pennsylvania and then the silver camps of Colorado and New Mexico, where Dafydd was a timberman. In 1879 a roof fell on him in the Consolidated's Number Two shaft at Plata Vieja. Thomasina did not go home. She opened a school in the camp for the miners' children, Mexican, Irish, Welsh, Black and German, taught them in three languages, preached in the stone schoolroom on Sundays to anyone who came, and became, without anyone voting for her, the person the miners go to when something is wrong. In 1881 something is. She is the voice of the miners' committee, and since the payroll was stolen she has been trying to keep three hundred and eighty hungry men from doing something stupid in either direction. (Companion. Hooks: the miners; the Company handbill; the schoolroom meeting; her union.)

dmNotes.roleplaying: Thomasina is the miners' conscience and the party's way into Plata Vieja. Use her to bring the Company's handbill to the party (st-scenario-002), to run the schoolroom meeting (st-scenario-003), and to ride at the head of the miners' column on election day. She is neither the plaza's nor the Company's. She is the miners', and she distrusts both towns, because neither has ever cared whether a miner's child ate. Her Fire and Brimstone works in a crowd, and on election day in Paragon a crowd is exactly where she will be. Steady can hold the miners, and Shake can break a lynch mob.
dmNotes.voice: A strong Welsh lilt in English, a schoolroom crispness, and Scripture used like a ruler across the knuckles. Calls grown men by their surnames and "boy" when they misbehave. Sings Welsh hymns under her breath when she is angry, which is often, and they are very beautiful.
dmNotes.motivations: Primary: get the miners paid and their children fed. Secondary: make sure nobody, the Company or the plaza, votes three hundred and eighty men like cattle. Tertiary: build her union, which she believes is God's work and which Hamish Gow believes is the devil's.
dmNotes.secrets: She knows that Hamish Gow gave Celestino Trujillo $300 for the People's ticket on 15 June, because Gow's clerk is her pupil's father, and she will tell the party, because she believes in plain dealing, before the Paragon Pioneer can. She has also been organising the miners into a local of the Knights of Labor, and the charter is in her Bible. If the Company finds out, it will use it to frighten Gow into helping them, and Gow will close the school.
dmNotes.attitude: Toward the party: brisk, testing, demanding proof; once convinced, an unshakeable ally. Toward Zadok Morgenstern, if played: her oldest friend in the camp; they argue about God every Saturday. Toward Celestino: she thinks him vain and honest, in that order. Toward Hamish Gow: a fair employer and a fool. Toward Fenton Rusk: she has met him once and recognised him at once, she says, as "a Pharisee in a straw hat". Toward Lysander Tolbert: the one man in the camp she treats as an equal.
